summary: Frontend-only testing of Live GPS tracker (/fitness/track) and Fitness Challenges (/fitness/challenges). Live GPS tracker flow PASSED end-to-end with simulated geolocation (start/move/accuracy/pause/resume/autosave/reload/resume-banner/restore/stop/discard). Challenges + session persistence BLOCKED by Firestore 'Missing or insufficient permissions' on both fitness_sessions and fitness_teams writes — this is a Firebase Console rules deployment issue (environment), confirmed in-UI with explicit error messages, per the main-agent note.

integration_issues.issue: Firestore writes to 'fitness_teams' return 'Missing or insufficient permissions.' — the error is surfaced inside the Create-team modal. Blocks ALL downstream challenge testing (no own team => CreateChallengeForm shows the 'go-create-team' fallback).

action_items: ENVIRONMENT (user/Firebase Console): Update Firestore security rules for `fitness_teams` and `fitness_sessions` so authenticated users can create/update their own team docs (createdBy==uid) and session docs (userId==uid). Current rules return permission-denied for both — the exact error 'Missing or insufficient permissions.' surfaces in the Create-team modal and in SaveForm's [data-testid=save-error]. This blocks the challenges/contributions acceptance criteria.

After rules deploy: re-run the Challenges acceptance set (create team -> create 100 km in 100 days challenge -> log 5 km manual session dated today -> verify preselected team toggle, counts-toward-challenge text, challenge card 5.0 km total and member 5.0/100). Everything that is testable without Firestore writes already passes.
critical_code_review_comments: FitnessTrackPage.jsx L580-596: SaveForm swallows the getDocs error on fitness_teams silently (setTeams([])). That is fine but can hide rules misconfigs; consider logging in dev mode.
FitnessChallengesPage.jsx L80-128: Guard on ownTeams.length===0 is correct and user-friendly.

No visible deviations from the stated spec: challengeWindow/challengeProgress math in challenges.js correctly computes targetKm = goalKm * members for 'individual' and uses sessionMs() for timestamp sources; splitSegments logic in RouteMap is not re-visited (previous iterations covered).
liveTracking.js useWakeLock cleanup correctly releases on unmount; onVis re-acquires on visibility — looks good.

success_rate.frontend: Live GPS 100% (all 14 acceptance criteria verified). Challenges/contribution flow BLOCKED by Firestore rules (0% executable, code paths look correct on inspection).

seed_data_creation: Attempted to create team 'TEST QA Team <ts>' at /fitness/teams; blocked by Firestore permissions so NO new docs created. Logged-in draft (fitness_live_draft in localStorage) was discarded at end of Live GPS run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live GPS is solid; banner km bug is fixed (verified 0.33 km, not 0.00). Challenge/contribution flow cannot be verified until Firestore rules for fitness_teams and fitness_sessions allow writes for the signed-in user. When rules are fixed, re-run: (a) create team at /fitness/teams, (b) create '100 km in 100 days' challenge from /fitness/challenges using preset-0, (c) log a 5 km manual session (team should be preselected, counts-toward-challenge text should appear), (d) verify challenge card totals/members, (e) verify /fitness active-challenges section + challenge-{id}-open link, (f) delete challenge for cleanup.
rca of the issue: Firestore security rules for 'fitness_teams' and 'fitness_sessions' are not in effect on the preview project (building-my-awesome-life). addDoc/updateDoc requests return permission-denied, surfaced to the UI as 'Missing or insufficient permissions.'. Reproduction: login as QA, go to /fitness/teams, click 'Create team', type a name, submit -> red error inside modal; or /fitness/track -> Manual tab -> fill 1km/10min -> Save session -> red [data-testid=save-error] shows the same text. Mitigation: deploy the committed rules in /app/firestore.rules (per /app/memory/test_credentials.md) to Firebase Console for the project, specifically adding create/update rules keyed on request.auth.uid for the two collections. No code change needed on the client.
